items.label: f02-footer-is-not-a-checksum
items.front: What does the END footer in the snapshot protect against, and what does it not prove?
items.back: It records the expected account and transaction counts, so a normally truncated or incomplete file is rejected. It is not a cryptographic integrity check and does not prove that balances reconcile with the history.

items.label: f03-reordering-two-writes
items.front: The old app saved accounts, then transactions, to separate files. Why does swapping the order not fix it?
items.back: Either order leaves a window where one file is newer than the other; swapping only changes which half can be stale. The fix is one write: both collections in one snapshot replaced atomically.

items.label: f01-zero-amounts
items.front: Where is zero allowed, and where is it refused, for money in the bank simulator?
items.back: An account balance may be zero (Money.nonNegative). A deposit, withdrawal or transfer amount must be greater than zero (Money.positive). The type BigDecimal alone does not capture that domain rule.

items.prompt: The same 5.00 transfer from Alice to Bob is made twice in one minute. How can storage tell which TRANSFER_IN goes with which TRANSFER_OUT?

choices.text: By timestamp, as both halves are created in the same millisecond
Not reliably, since nothing but the reciprocal account ids links them
By the transaction ids, as each IN id is its OUT id plus one
By the shared transfer id that is written to both halves of every transfer

choices: By timestamp, as both halves are created in the same millisecond
Not reliably, since nothing but the reciprocal account ids links them
By the transaction ids, as each IN id is its OUT id plus one
By the shared transfer id that is written to both halves of every transfer

items.explanation: createTransaction gives each record its own TXN-UUID and its own LocalDateTime.now(); the only link is the reciprocal account id. 02 names this limit; a correlation id is practice exercise 4.

items.prompt: Account A holds 10.00. A caller does service.getAccountById("A").increaseBalance(new BigDecimal("5.00")). What does the service report for A afterwards?

choices.text: 15.00 with a deposit row, as increaseBalance records a matching transaction
10.00 and unchanged history, as the caller changed a detached copy
15.00 with no new history, as the caller holds the service's own account object
An IllegalStateException, since accounts handed out by reads are read-only

choices: 15.00 with a deposit row, as increaseBalance records a matching transaction
10.00 and unchanged history, as the caller changed a detached copy
15.00 with no new history, as the caller holds the service's own account object
An IllegalStateException, since accounts handed out by reads are read-only

items.explanation: getAccountById returns account.copy(). BankAccount is still mutable, so the call succeeds, but on the copy. The regression test rereads the service and expects 10.00.

items.prompt: A valid snapshot gets one extra line, broken, appended after its END footer. Which error does the next startup report?

choices.text: An unsupported header error, as the file no longer ends with a footer
No error, as lines after the footer are ignored by the loader
A footer error, as the last line no longer has END and the two counts
An invalid record on the old footer line, as END is read as an unknown record

choices: An unsupported header error, as the file no longer ends with a footer
No error, as lines after the footer are ignored by the loader
A footer error, as the last line no longer has END and the two counts
An invalid record on the old footer line, as END is read as an unknown record

items.explanation: The loader treats only the last line as the footer and parses everything between header and last line as records. The old END line is now in that range and fails as "Unknown record type", reported as "Invalid bank snapshot record on line N." Verified in a probe.

items.prompt: transfer("X", "X", 1.00, "") is called, and no account X exists. Which message does it throw?

choices.text: You cannot transfer money to the same account.
Account not found: X
Source and destination account ids are required.
Insufficient balance for this transfer.

choices: You cannot transfer money to the same account.
Account not found: X
Source and destination account ids are required.
Insufficient balance for this transfer.

items.explanation: transfer checks for nulls, then for equal ids, and only after that calls requireAccount. So the same-account rule fires before the missing account is noticed. Verified in a probe.

items.prompt: A data directory holds accounts.txt but no transactions.txt and no bank.snapshot.txt. What does startup do?

choices.text: Refuses with an incomplete-legacy-data error before any menu appears
Loads the accounts with an empty history, then writes a fresh snapshot
Ignores accounts.txt and always starts a new, empty bank there
Loads the accounts and creates transactions.txt on the first save

choices: Refuses with an incomplete-legacy-data error before any menu appears
Loads the accounts with an empty history, then writes a fresh snapshot
Ignores accounts.txt and always starts a new, empty bank there
Loads the accounts and creates transactions.txt on the first save

items.explanation: loadSnapshot throws "Incomplete legacy data: both accounts.txt and transactions.txt are required." when exactly one legacy file exists. Verified in a probe.

items.prompt: Bob received a 2.50 transfer and later withdrew it, so his balance is 0.00. The user picks menu 9 for Bob and types yes. What happens?

choices.text: Refused, as its transaction history protects it from deletion
Bob is deleted and the transfer is reversed back to Alice
Bob is deleted along with his history, and Alice's transfer row stays
Bob is deleted, as a zero balance is all that deletion requires

choices: Refused, as its transaction history protects it from deletion
Bob is deleted and the transfer is reversed back to Alice
Bob is deleted along with his history, and Alice's transfer row stays
Bob is deleted, as a zero balance is all that deletion requires

items.explanation: deleteUnusedAccount throws "Only a zero-balance account with no transaction history can be deleted." when any transaction names the account. Verified in a probe.

items.prompt: The original getAllAccounts returned a new list. Why did that not stop callers from changing service balances?

choices.text: The new list still held the same mutable account objects the service used
Callers could cast the copied list back to the internal LinkedHashMap
Callers could add accounts to the copy, and every one was saved on exit
The list was copied lazily, so it was still shared until it was first read

choices: The new list still held the same mutable account objects the service used
Callers could cast the copied list back to the internal LinkedHashMap
Callers could add accounts to the copy, and every one was saved on exit
The list was copied lazily, so it was still shared until it was first read

items.explanation: Copying a list copies the references, not the elements. The fix copies each account (account.copy()) on every outward read.

items.prompt: The snapshot's first line is the word garbage. The app prints a load error and stops. What exit status does the java process return?

choices.text: A non-zero status, as the uncaught IOException ends the JVM
1, as main calls System.exit(1) after printing the load error
0, as main catches the IOException, prints it and returns normally
2, as a corrupt data file is reported with its own exit code

choices: A non-zero status, as the uncaught IOException ends the JVM
1, as main calls System.exit(1) after printing the load error
0, as main catches the IOException, prints it and returns normally
2, as a corrupt data file is reported with its own exit code

items.explanation: main wraps construction and run in try/catch(IOException), prints "Failed to load or save bank data: ..." and falls off the end. Verified by running the CLI: exit=0.

items.prompt: A directory holds valid accounts.txt and transactions.txt and no snapshot. The app makes one deposit and saves. What is on disk afterwards?

choices.text: The two legacy files rewritten in place, and no snapshot file created yet
A new bank.snapshot.txt, with the two legacy files renamed to .bak copies
A new bank.snapshot.txt, with both legacy files left exactly as they were
bank.snapshot.txt replaces both legacy files, which are deleted after the move

choices: The two legacy files rewritten in place, and no snapshot file created yet
A new bank.snapshot.txt, with the two legacy files renamed to .bak copies
A new bank.snapshot.txt, with both legacy files left exactly as they were
bank.snapshot.txt replaces both legacy files, which are deleted after the move

items.explanation: Legacy files are only read for migration. saveSnapshot writes bank.snapshot.txt, which is authoritative from then on; the test checks accounts.txt is unchanged and that later edits to it are ignored.

items.prompt: An account holds 10.00. Eight threads submit 64 withdrawals of 1.00 to one BankService at the same moment. How many succeed?

choices.text: Exactly 10, as withdraw is synchronized on the service instance
None, since concurrent withdrawals on one account are refused outright
All 64, with the balance going negative until the next save validates it
Usually more than 10, as each check of the balance races with the debit

choices: Exactly 10, as withdraw is synchronized on the service instance
None, since concurrent withdrawals on one account are refused outright
All 64, with the balance going negative until the next save validates it
Usually more than 10, as each check of the balance races with the debit

items.explanation: withdraw checks the balance and debits inside one synchronized method, so the check-then-act cannot interleave. The regression test asserts 10 successes, balance 0.00 and 10 history rows.

items.prompt: Two app processes open the same data directory. The second creates Bob and exits; then the first creates Alice and exits. What does the snapshot hold?

choices.text: Alice alone, as the first process rewrites the file from its own state
Bob only, as the first process notices the newer file and gives up
Neither, as the clash leaves a corrupt snapshot that is then rejected
Alice and Bob, as each save merges its accounts into the existing file

choices: Alice alone, as the first process rewrites the file from its own state
Bob only, as the first process notices the newer file and gives up
Neither, as the clash leaves a corrupt snapshot that is then rejected
Alice and Bob, as each save merges its accounts into the existing file

items.explanation: Each process loads once and saveSnapshot replaces the whole file without comparing it to what is on disk. synchronized only protects one JVM. The trace lab reproduces this lost update.

items.prompt: In menu 3 the user deposits 1.001 into an account holding 10.00. What does the CLI print, and what is the balance?

choices.text: Deposit recorded, and the balance becomes 11.00 after rounding to two places
Operation failed: Please enter a valid number for the amount. It stays 10.00
Deposit recorded, and the balance becomes 11.001 because BigDecimal is exact
Operation failed: Deposit: Amount must use at most 2 decimal places. It stays 10.00

choices: Deposit recorded, and the balance becomes 11.00 after rounding to two places
Operation failed: Please enter a valid number for the amount. It stays 10.00
Deposit recorded, and the balance becomes 11.001 because BigDecimal is exact
Operation failed: Deposit: Amount must use at most 2 decimal places. It stays 10.00

items.explanation: readAmount parses 1.001 fine; Money.nonNegative uses setScale(2, UNNECESSARY), which throws, and validateAmount prefixes "Deposit: ". The menu loop prints "Operation failed: ". Nothing was mutated.

items.prompt: A deposit succeeds in memory, then saveData throws IOException because the disk is full. What does the CLI do next?

choices.text: It shows the menu again with the deposit kept, waiting for a later save
It prints "Operation failed:", rolls the deposit back and shows the menu again
It leaves the menu, prints the save error, and skips the success line
It prints the success line, then retries the save when the user exits with 7

choices: It shows the menu again with the deposit kept, waiting for a later save
It prints "Operation failed:", rolls the deposit back and shows the menu again
It leaves the menu, prints the save error, and skips the success line
It prints the success line, then retries the save when the user exits with 7

items.explanation: The menu loop catches only IllegalArgumentException and IllegalStateException, so the IOException escapes run and main prints "Failed to load or save bank data: ...". The deposit had already changed memory; nothing rolls it back.
